sections.h2: What are the options for filing a deed with Allegan County?
sections.html:
Paper and electronic filing both work. The register's page lists three e-recording vendors with direct lines: CSC (866-652-0111), Simplifile (800-460-5657) and ePN, the E-Recording Partners Network (888-325-3365). Title companies normally use one of these, which spares most sellers any contact with them.

The same page links a land records search portal, the state recording requirements and county clerk and register annual reports. After filing, the register enters the paper in a book called a liber and stamps that reference on the document. An image becomes the permanent record, and the office does not keep the original deed or mortgage.

Counter staff do not prepare documents or answer legal questions, and they refer people to an attorney or title company. One protection for senders comes from MCL 565.201: a register may not refuse a compliant paper over its wording, and a paper already recorded is presumed to comply. The format rules are the real hurdle, so let the title agent look over the deed before signing.

sections.h2: What are Allegan County's recording and copy fees?
sections.html:
One flat $30 covers a recording of any length, as MCL 600.2567 provides. The remaining items on the statutory list are short.

  • $3 on top for every further instrument that a single paper assigns or discharges.
  • $1 per page of copies, and a $5 certification charge.
  • Grantor and grantee searches at 50 cents per year examined, minimum $5.
  • $1 for filing or looking up any other paper.

Fees are due when the paper is left. For electronic filings the fee can follow electronically, up to one business day after receipt. For copy purposes, a "page" is one side of a sheet measuring 8 1/2 by 11 up to 14 inches, in paper of 20 pound weight or more.

sections.h2: How much transfer tax is due on an Allegan County sale?
sections.html:
A median Allegan County home is worth $267,100 by Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024, well above Alcona County's $162,800 and Alpena County's $153,900. Across the two taxes the seller pays $4.30 for each $500 of value, rounding a partial $500 upward.

Transfer tax at three Allegan County sale prices, from the $0.55 county rate (MCL 207.504) and $3.75 state rate (MCL 207.525)
Sale priceCountyStateCombined
$200,000$220.00$1,500.00$1,720.00
$267,100 (median)$294.25$2,006.25$2,300.50
$350,000$385.00$2,625.00$3,010.00

The seller carries liability under MCL 207.523, although a buyer may pay on the seller's behalf. Payment reaches the county treasurer no later than 15 days after the instrument is delivered.

sections.h2: Which Allegan County transfers can skip the tax?
sections.html:
MCL 207.526 exempts a list of transfers, and a few come up often with houses in a lake or farm county like this one.

  • A deed that only straightens a boundary line when no money changes hands.
  • A quitclaim deed given to confirm a title the grantee already holds, such as one that corrects a flaw.
  • A transfer between a limited liability company and its members when ownership shares are unchanged.
  • A transfer between a partnership and its partners on the same terms.
  • A deed in which the grantor is a government body or officer acting officially.

Anyone relying on one of these should say so to the title agent before closing. A refund request goes to the Department of Treasury.

sections.h2: What other services does the Allegan County register offer owners?
sections.html:
The office runs a free Property Fraud Alert. An owner or business enters a name and gets a notice whenever a recorded document matches it, which gives early warning of a forged deed or a lien filed against you.

The register also posts Plat Board public notices, which matter to anyone splitting a parcel before a sale. A related treasurer form covers tax certification for land divisions and lot line adjustments, with its own instructions.

U.S. passport applications are taken at the office by appointment only, between 8 a.m. and 4 p.m. on weekdays. The number to call is 269-673-0390.

sections.h2: What does the Allegan County Treasurer handle in a sale?
sections.html:
The Treasurer's Office certifies deeds, keeps tax histories, and collects delinquent real estate tax for the 35 townships, cities and villages in the county. The county chose to run the whole tax reversion process in-house, including title searches, court hearings, foreclosure and sale.

A seller with delinquent tax should talk to the treasurer's staff first, because the office advances delinquent amounts to the local units through its revolving fund. The page links to pay delinquent taxes, search tax records and foreclosure sales.

The treasurer also describes how former owners can claim leftover foreclosure proceeds. For foreclosures starting in 2021, a person with title or equity must file Form 5743 with the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 after the auctions with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow between February 1 and May 15. These steps come from MCL 211.78t.

sections.h2: Who sets and bills property tax in Allegan County?
sections.html:
Assessing happens at the township or city level, with the county Equalization Department publishing property records, a township and city assessor list, equalization reports and a tax levies and millages page. The county treasurer's page describes accounting for tax collections of the 35 local units and collecting delinquent real estate tax.

Because 24 townships, 9 cities and 2 villages each act as their own unit, the correct office depends on the parcel. The county's directory lists addresses and phone lines for all of them, such as Allegan Township at 269-673-5051, Otsego City Hall at 269-692-3391 and Holland City Hall at 616-355-1300.

Ask your township or city for the current tax balance before you list the house.

sections.h2: What is Allegan County like for a seller?
sections.html:
Allegan County was laid out in 1831 and organized in 1835. The county seat is the city of Allegan, and Holland is the largest city. It covers 825 square miles of land and counts as the Holland micropolitan area, part of the Grand Rapids combined area. The area is mostly agricultural and is urbanizing as Grand Rapids and Kalamazoo spread toward it.

The Lake Michigan shore draws vacation homes, especially around Saugatuck and Douglas. The Allegan State Game Area covers about 45,000 acres, Saugatuck Dunes State Park has dune trails and a swim beach, and Lake Allegan is another destination. A Pottawatomi band, the Match-e-be-nash-she-wish Band, has a reservation in the county.

The 2025 Census estimate is 123,188 residents, up 2.2 percent from April 2020. Owners live in 87.4 percent of homes, median household income is $83,283, and the mean commute is 24.2 minutes. The county issued 399 building permits in 2025.

sections.h2: What do household and business numbers show for Allegan County?
sections.html:
For 2020 to 2024 the Census Bureau counts 45,522 households averaging 2.64 people. Owners with a mortgage report median monthly costs of $1,523, owners with none $575, and median gross rent is $1,100. About 92.2 percent of residents lived in the same house a year earlier, and 4,920 residents are veterans.

The county had 2,571 employer establishments and 38,899 jobs in 2023, a 5.8 percent drop in employment from 2022. Retail sales reached about $1.68 billion in 2022, or $13,863 per resident, and the poverty rate is 8.2 percent.

faqs.q: Which e-recording services does Allegan County accept?
faqs.a: It accepts CSC, Simplifile and ePN. Their phone lines are 866-652-0111, 800-460-5657 and 888-325-3365.

faqs.q: How much does a deed cost to record in Allegan County?
faqs.a: A recording costs $30 per document. Add $3 per further instrument assigned or discharged, $1 a page for copies and $5 for certification.

faqs.q: What is the state share of transfer tax on a $267,100 Allegan County house?
faqs.a: The state share is $2,006.25, computed on 535 units of $500 at $3.75. With the $294.25 county share, the seller owes $2,300.50.

faqs.q: Will the Allegan County register prepare my deed?
faqs.a: No. The office neither drafts documents nor answers legal questions, so an attorney or title company must do that.

faqs.q: How does a former owner claim surplus from an Allegan County foreclosure sale?
faqs.a: Send Form 5743 to the county treasurer by July 1 of the foreclosure year. The county replies by January 31 with Form 5744, and a court motion may follow.
